newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz says mulling new lira bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says mulling new lira bond issue.

text.p: After making a successful debut in the Italian lira market late last year, Mexico's federal government is considering placing another lira-denominated bond, the finance minister said on Tuesday.

"We still don't have any date for this, but the lira market has been an attractive market in the last months. In the last months, there have been issuers in emerging countries, particularly Argentina, who have been active in the lira market," Guillermo Ortiz said.

The United Mexican States has debt amortizations of a little more than $1.4 billion in 1997, but analysts expect the government to go to the market to meet debt needs in 1998 and 1999, or to buy back more of its outstanding Brady Bonds.

The federal government placed a $1.0 billion 10-year global bond issue last week to cover most of its debt coming due this year, and the lira issue is seen covering the remainder needed for maturing paper this year.

Analysts have said the government is racing early this year to cover much of its debt needs, taking advantage of good global liquidity and a breathing space before key mid-term elections in Mexico in July that could shake up financial markets.
The last Mexican lira bond was a floating rate issue that paid three-month Libor plus 200 basis points, which was equivalent to 249 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Argentina launched a seven-year 500 billion lira issue in mid-October.
Syndicate managers in Europe have said the United Mexican States could launch a 500 billion 10-year Eurobond lira issue at the end of January or early Februry.
The government placed its first lira issue in November last year, worth 500 billion lira ($325 million), as part of its strategy to create new benchmarks in European currencies.
"We did a small issue last year, and certainly we will be exploring opportunities in this market in the future," Ortiz told reporters.
Chase Manhattan Corp was tipped to be the lead manager for the new issue.
